sentences.text: Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of both counsel, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This miscellaneous first appeal is filed by petitioner under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short), seeking enhancement of compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident dated 28.01.2016.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.

4. It is the case of the petitioner that on 28.01.2016 at about 7-30 p.m. he was riding motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-29/Y-9808 ('motorcycle' for short) and proceeding from Babaleshwar side towards Nidoni.

When he was near the land of Devanand Aladond on Babaleshwar-Nidoni road, a Mahindra Pickup Goods Van bearing registration KA-28/B-1186 (for short 'offending vehicle') came from opposite side, in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle.
In the said accident, petitioner sustained grievous injuries resulting in permanent partial disability.
Despite prolonged treatment, he is not completely cured.
As the owner and insurer, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
5. Before the Tribunal, respondent No.1 has remained ex parte.

6. Respondent No.2 filed written statement disputing that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the age, occupation, income of the petitioner, nature of the injuries sustained by him and that they have resulted in permanent partial disability and also the medical expenses incurred for the treatment.
At the time of accident, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence and therefore, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.
7. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal has framed the necessary issues.
8. Petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 and the doctor as P.W.2.
He has relied upon Exs.P.1 to 27.

2 9.

Respondent No.2 has not led any oral evidence, but got marked copy of insurance policy as Ex.R.1.
10.

Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by granting compensation in a sum of Rs.5,81,600/- and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same with interest at 6% per annum as detailed below:
 Nature of the heads Compensation  Pain and sufferings Rs.30,000/-
 Medical expenses Rs.3,00,000/-
 Loss of income due to Rs.2,01,600/-
 functional physical  disability  Food and nourishment Rs.10,000/-
 Attendant charges Rs.10,000/-
 Conveyance charges Rs.10,000/-
 Loss of amenities and Rs.20,000/-
 future unhappiness  Total 5,81,600/-
11.
Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
12. During the course of arguments, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the notional income taken at Rs.7,000/- p.m. is on the lower side.
Having regard to the nature of the injuries suffered, the disability taken at 15% is on the lower side.
The compensation granted under all the heads is also on the lower side and requires enhancement and prays to allow the appeal.
13. On the other hand learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and ward and prays to dismiss the appeal.

14. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for respondent No.2 and perused the records.
15.

Having regard to the fact that the respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award, the findings of the Tribunal that accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, petitioner sustained injuries and they have resulted in permanent partial disability has attained finality.
16. Based on the material on record, the Tribunal has correctly taken the age of the petitioner as 35 years and accordingly 16 is the appropriate multiplier.
In the absence of proof of exact income, the Tribunal has taken the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.7,000/.
Since the accident is of the year 2016, based on minimum wages, it ought to have taken at Rs.8,750/-.

Though P.W.2 has deposed that the petitioner has suffered permanent partial disability to the extent of 60% to whole body, having regard to the fact that he is not a treating doctor and taking into consideration the Huvanna vs Suresh And Anr on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74454047/
3 nature of injuries suffered, it would be appropriate to take the whole body disability at 20% instead of 15%.
With these components, the loss of income due to functional disability is Rs.8,750 x 12 x 16 x 20% = Rs.3,36,000/- as against Rs.2,01,600/- granted by the Tribunal.
17. Based on the medial bills, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- and it requires no interference.
In the same manner, compensation granted in a sum of Rs.10,000/- each under the head food & nourishment, attendant charges and conveyance charges is also that reasonable.
It also does not require any inference.

However, having regard to the nature of the injuries suffered and also that they have resulted in permanent partial disability,
compensation granted in a sum of Rs.30,000/- under the head pain and suffering is enhanced to Rs.40,000/- and Rs.20,000/- granted under the head loss of amenities is enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.

18. Thus, in all the petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.7,36,000/- together with interest at 6% p.a. as against Rs.5,81,600/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:

19. Of course as the insurer of the offending vehicle, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the enhanced compensation with accrued interest.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Appeal is allowed in part.
